newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA STICK WITH TAYLOR, DEMOTE HEALY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA STICK WITH TAYLOR, DEMOTE HEALY.

text.p: Australian cricket selectors kept faith with embattled captain Mark Taylor on Thursday for the forthcoming Ashes test series against England.
But his deputy, wicket-keeper Ian Healy, was demoted in favour of all-rounder Steve Waugh -- confirming Waugh's status as Taylor's natural successor.

Taylor, whose position as opener was in question after a lengthy form slump, will lead Australia's 17-man squad when they leave next month for the six-test series and said he expected to last out the tour as captain.
"I have been appointed for the tour of England and I'm looking forward to playing six test matches as captain," Taylor told a news conference after the team announcement.
Selectors dropped batsman Matthew Hayden and pace bowler Paul Reiffel from the squad which completed a 2-1 test series defeat over South Africa last month.
Opener Michael Slater, dynamic young batsman Ricky Ponting and Queensland state paceman Michael Kasprowicz were recalled.

Ponting was dropped after the second test against West Indies last December but shone in the domestic Sheffield Shield competition. Kasprowicz led the domestic tallies with 48 wickets, although the burly Queenslander went wicketless in his first two tests in the recent series against West Indies.
Slater began his test career in England in 1993 and averaged 47.41 before being dropped last year.
But Healy's demotion was the biggest surprise in the squad after weeks of speculation that Taylor would be ousted after a test run drought stretching back to late 1995.
Healy became the first Australian to be suspended under the International Cricket Council's code of conduct when he was put out for two matches for dissent during the South African tour.
Healy was suspended after questioning his dismissal in the third test against South Africa in Pretoria and then throwing his bat as he reached the Australian dressing room.
Despite his run-in with authorities, Healy went on to captain Australia in the limited-overs series against the South Africans after Taylor stood aside after the first two matches.
Waugh captained Australia for the first time in the final limited overs match last week, which South Africa won to restrict Australia to a 4-3 series win.
Waugh, 31, is Australia's most experienced player and regarded by many observers as the best batsman in the world.
The only player in the squad not to have played test cricket is Adam Gilchrist, the man being groomed to take over from Healy when the combative Queenslander retires.
A dashing left-handed batsman, Gilchrist was added to the Australian squad for the limited overs series against South Africa and made several telling contributions with the bat.

Under Taylor's aggressive leadership, Australia have become the unofficial world champions of test cricket, beating West Indies at home and away, South Africa away and England, Pakistan and Sri Lanka at home.
Squad:
Batsmen - Mark Taylor (captain), Mark Waugh, Steve Waugh (vice-captain), Matthew Elliott, Michael Slater, Ricky Ponting, Justin Langer.
All-rounders: Greg Blewett, Michael Bevan,
Wicketkeepers: Ian Healy, Adam Gilchrist
Bowlers: Glenn McGrath, Jason Gillespie, Andy Bichel, Shane Warne, Michael Kasprowicz, Brendon Julian.
